heading: INT. BOWLING ALLEY SNACK COUNTER - AFTERNOON

units.text: INT. BOWLING ALLEY SNACK COUNTER - AFTERNOON
A sleepy league day.
The pins clatter in the distance like a slow applause.
Five people share a booth built for four.
PRISCILLA "PIP" NAKASHIMA (30s, team captain, sunburnt nose) stirs a milkshake with great concentration.
Next to her, her husband WALTER GRUNDY-BELL (30s, wearing a shirt that says BOWL OR DIE) eats nachos one chip at a time.
Across the table, her brother OTIS (20s, hoodie, headphones) stares into his phone.
Squeezed at the end are the Pellegrinos: elderly twins CARMELA and CORRADO PELLEGRINO (70s, matching cardigans), who have been bowling together since the Truman administration.
Walter, you promised you'd bowl a hundred.
units.name: PIP

units.text: I bowled ninety-eight, Pip.
units.name: WALTER

units.text: That's two short.
units.name: PIP

units.text: It was a very good ninety-eight.
units.name: WALTER

units.text: It was a gutter and a prayer.
units.name: OTIS

units.text: Corrado, pass the salt.
units.name: CARMELA

units.text: Carmela, you don't need salt.
units.name: CORRADO

units.text: I need what I need.
units.name: CARMELA

units.text: Corrado slides the shaker across the table.
Carmela and Walter both reach for it at the same time and knock the nachos into Pip's lap.
All five freeze.
Walter.
units.name: PIP

units.text: I'll get napkins.
units.name: WALTER

units.text: Carmela, you did that.
units.name: CORRADO

units.text: I did not.
units.name: CARMELA

units.text: Otis finally lifts his eyes from the phone, examines the carnage, and returns to the screen without a word.
Pip dabs cheese from her knee and takes a slow, controlled sip of milkshake.
Next frame, Walter. Hundred or nothing.
units.name: PIP
